title: unified-rollouts: improve canary/A-B/shadow auto-rollback with metric quorums and stability windows
author: Priya Desai
description: Context: we continue to harden unified rollouts for production traffic patterns where short-term metric noise and skew across regions cause spurious auto-rollbacks. This PR introduces two complementary safety improvements: 1) a metric quorum requirement for auto-rollback decisions (reduce sensitivity to single-metric flukes across probes), and 2) a configurable stability window that delays final rollback decisions until short transient anomalies clear. Motivation: recent incidents (SUP-9081) showed that a single availability probe in a low-volume probing stage could trigger rollback for canary/shadow traffic even when overall traffic and other metrics were healthy. The current autorollback logic naively aggregates metrics and makes a decision per stage without considering quorum or stability. Changes: - Add quorum-based evaluation across probe/metric groups: configure "metric_quorum" as a percentage (default 66%) of metrics that must breach thresholds to count toward rollback. - Add "stability_window_seconds" parameter per rollout stage: measurements must persist for the window before counting as a decisive breach. - Update the autorollback engine to support weighted metrics and explicit ignore-lists for noisy probes. - Add telemetry: rollout.rollback_candidates, rollout.quorum_evaluation, rollout.stability_delay_seconds for tracing decisions. - Expose new fields in the rollout API and Console UI: metric_quorum, stability_window_seconds, metric_weights, noise_filter_patterns. - Backwards compatible: if new fields are unset, behavior defaults to prior logic (quorum=100%, stability_window=0s). Implementation notes: - The core decision engine (rollout/engine.go) now computes per-metric sliding windows and runs quorum checks; uses existing metrics ingestion pipeline and reuses the probe-sampling code. - Added unit and integration tests including e2e scenarios that simulate intermittent probe failures. - Updated rollout admission and validation logic to prevent unsafe configs (e.g., quorum < 50% for critical stages is rejected by validation). Checklist: - [x] Design doc linked in Linear ENG-4471 - [x] Unit tests added - [x] Integration e2e tests added - [x] Console UI fields and help text updated - [x] Feature flags added (rollout.autorollback.quorum_enabled) - [x] Telemetry dashboards updated - [x] Backcompat verified Rollout plan: feature gated behind rollout.autorollback.quorum_enabled; will enable for internal dogfood first and then customer opt-in release. Observability: added dashboards and alerts to detect cases where stability_window is delaying rollbacks unexpectedly. Backwards compatibility: defaults preserve prior behavior. Risks and mitigations: - Misconfigured low quorum could delay necessary rollbacks: validation and safe defaults mitigate. - Additional CPU for sliding windows in very large rollouts: implementation uses approximate counters and configurable sampling. Testing: ran canary e2e against staging with synthetic noise; verified no false positive rollbacks across 1000 simulated probes. Related PRs: links to prior auto-rollback refactor and observability PRs are included in commits and comments.
